Show vendors and contracts.
For Lakeshore Holdings, eight named vendor relationships are confirmed across cloud, finance, HR, treasury, and AI infrastructure.
- **Microsoft carries the only high-risk contract** — renewing June 2027, it spans cloud, identity, productivity, and AI, making it the broadest single dependency in the portfolio and the relationship with the most at stake if terms drift.
- **Three contracts expire before year-end 2026** — Kyriba (September), Ironclad and ServiceNow (both November), and Oracle (December) create a concentrated renewal window that warrants sequencing decisions now, not at notice date.
- **The portfolio is otherwise stable** — Workday, DealCloud, and Databricks carry medium or low risk with 2027 renewals, suggesting manageable exposure once the 2026 cluster is addressed.
Annual cost is not confirmed in current business context; commercial sizing should be validated before any negotiation posture is set.
| Vendor | Service | Renewal | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft | Cloud, identity, productivity, and AI | 2027-06-30 | High |
| Oracle | ERP and database services | 2026-12-31 | Medium |
| ServiceNow | ITSM and AI governance workflow | 2026-11-30 | Medium |
| Ironclad | Contract lifecycle management | 2026-11-30 | Medium |
| Kyriba | Treasury workstation and bank connectivity | 2026-09-30 | Medium |
| Workday | HCM and finance SaaS | 2027-02-28 | Medium |
| Databricks | AI and analytics workspace | 2027-01-31 | Medium |
| DealCloud | Portfolio CRM and investment pipeline | 2027-04-30 | Low |
**Branch:** Tower — spend exposure and prioritization. Source — Microsoft and the 2026 cluster as renewal-risk candidates for commercial validation. Intelligence — tradeoffs on Microsoft consolidation vs. diversification.
Moves — sequencing the 2026 renewal window.
